subtitle: From Shattered Palace to Silent Laboratory: A King’s Hidden Gift

panels.shot: wide, dramatic three-quarter view of Radha Kishore Manikya silhouetted against the gleaming domes of Ujjayanta Palace, with a faint overlay hint of a laboratory table in the clouds above
panels.action: Radha Kishore Manikya stands in regal pose before the freshly built Ujjayanta Palace, one hand resting on a rolled architectural plan while the hazy outline of scientific instruments floats ghostlike in the background sky.

dialogue.text: At the turn of a trembling century, Radha Kishore Manikya rebuilt his shattered capital—and, in quiet shadows, helped keep Jagadish Chandra Bose’s science alive.

i18n.hi: काँपती सदी की दहलीज़ पर राधा किशोर माणिक्य ने बिखरी राजधानी फिर बनाई—और चुपचाप, जगदीश चंद्र बोस की विज्ञान साधना को साँसें दीं।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of Agartala during the 1897 Assam earthquake
panels.action: Buildings sway and crack in Agartala as the earth shudders; Radha Kishore Manikya, in royal attire, stands on a balcony gripping the railing, watching dust rise from damaged palace structures.

dialogue.text: In June 1897, the great Assam earthquake shook the hills of Tripura, cracking the old royal quarters and toppling walls that had stood for generations.

i18n.hi: जून 1897 में असम के भीषण भूकम्प ने त्रिपुरा की पहाड़ियों को हिला दिया, पुराने राजमहल में दरारें डाल दीं और पीढ़ियों से खड़ी दीवारें गिरा दीं।

panels.shot: medium close-up, low angle, focusing on Radha Kishore amidst rubble
panels.action: Radha Kishore Manikya stands amidst fallen plaster and broken columns in the old palace courtyard, dust in the air, surveying the damage with a calm but resolute expression.

dialogue.text: For the Manikya king, the cracked palace was more than broken brick; it was a question: would Tripura cling to the past, or rise in a new form?

i18n.hi: माणिक्य राजा के लिए टूटा महल बस ईंट नहीं था; ये सवाल था—त्रिपुरा अतीत से चिपकेगा या नए रूप में उठेगा?

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a council chamber
panels.action: In a high-ceilinged chamber, Radha Kishore Manikya studies detailed architectural drawings laid on a long table, alongside British architects from a firm like Martin and Burn, as attendants stand respectfully behind.

dialogue.text: Radha Kishore turned to the Calcutta firm Martin and Burn, commissioning a new palace—one that would carry Tripura into the age of railways, telegraphs and Indo-Saracenic stone.

i18n.hi: राधा किशोर ने कलकत्ता की मार्टिन एंड बर्न फर्म को बुलाया, नया महल बनवाने को—जो त्रिपुरा को रेल, टेलीग्राफ और इंडो–सरसेनिक पत्थरों के दौर में ले जाए।

panels.action: The rising skeleton of Ujjayanta Palace dominates the frame; scaffolding clings to domes and arches, labourers haul stone, while Radha Kishore Manikya on horseback inspects the site under a bright sky.

dialogue.text: By 1899, the flat lands beside the Haora River echoed with hammers and shouted orders, as domes, verandahs and a grand durbar hall climbed from the dust.

i18n.hi: 1899 तक हाओरा नदी के किनारे समतल ज़मीन हथौड़ों की चोट और अफ़सरों की पुकार से गूँज उठी, जब गुम्बद, बरामदे और भव्य दरबार हॉल धूल से उगने लगे।

panels.shot: sunset wide of completed palace and gardens
panels.action: The completed Ujjayanta Palace gleams with twin domes, central entrance and reflective ponds in the formal gardens; Radha Kishore Manikya walks along a pathway, silhouetted against the water and fountains.

dialogue.text: Between 1899 and 1901, the new Ujjayanta Palace rose in white symmetry—domes mirrored in long ponds, gardens laid with geometries of power and order.

i18n.hi: 1899 से 1901 के बीच नया उज्जयंत महल सफ़ेद समरूपता में उठा—लंबी पोखरों में झरते गुम्बद, सत्ता और अनुशासन की ज्यामितीय बाग़वानी के साथ।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of the durbar hall
panels.action: Inside the durbar hall, high arches and chandeliers frame Radha Kishore Manikya seated on a throne-like chair; officials stand in rows, with separate tables for police and revenue officers indicating administrative reforms.

dialogue.text: Within its halls, he separated police from revenue, reorganised offices and turned the quake’s chaos into a more layered, modern administration.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं दालानों में उसने पुलिस और राजस्व को अलग किया, दफ़्तरों को फिर से सजाया और भूकम्प की अव्यवस्था को परतदार, आधुनिक शासन में बदला।

panels.action: Radha Kishore Manikya sits at a heavy desk in a palace study, surrounded by files and letters; one pile bears seals of schools, hospitals and Visva-Bharati, suggesting grants and donations.

dialogue.text: He sent funds to schools and medical institutions, and, later, to Rabindranath Tagore’s Visva-Bharati—seeing knowledge as another pillar for his fragile frontier state.

i18n.hi: उसने स्कूलों और चिकित्सालयों को धन भेजा, और बाद में रवीन्द्रनाथ ठाकुर के विश्वभारती को भी—ज्ञान को अपने नाज़ुक सीमांत राज्य का दूसरा खम्भा मानते हुए।

panels.shot: transition shot, wide, of colonial Calcutta street
panels.action: A busy Calcutta street scene shows horse-drawn carriages, tram tracks, and the façade of a colonial-era academic building, hinting at the University of Calcutta’s science facilities.

dialogue.text: While Agartala remade itself in plaster and pond, in Calcutta another battle unfolded—this one fought with coils, metals and tiny sparks.

i18n.hi: जब अगरतला प्लास्टर और तालाबों में खुद को गढ़ रहा था, तब कलकत्ता में एक और जंग चल रही थी—ये वाली तारों, धातुओं और नन्हीं चिनगारियों से लड़ी गई।

panels.action: Inside a modest laboratory, early radio and experimental equipment lie on a crowded bench—coils, metal plates and delicate glass—not clearly showing Bose, but evoking his workspace’s strain and scarcity.

dialogue.text: Jagadish Chandra Bose worked in such rooms, probing wireless signals and plant responses, often with limited pay, modest apparatus and doubts from colonial officials.

i18n.hi: जगदीश चंद्र बोस ऐसे ही कमरों में काम करते, वायरलेस संकेतों और पौधों की प्रतिक्रिया टटोलते—अक्सर कम वेतन, साधारण यंत्र और हुकूमत के शक भरे सवालों के बीच।

panels.shot: medium shot in palace with letter in hand
panels.action: In Agartala, Radha Kishore Manikya sits by a window overlooking the palace ponds, reading a letter closely; his face shows thoughtful concern as an attendant waits discreetly behind.

dialogue.text: Correspondence preserved in later archives hints that letters crossed the distance—Carried news of Bose’s struggles into the quiet corridors of Ujjayanta.

i18n.hi: बाद के अभिलेखों में बची चिट्ठियाँ इशारा करती हैं कि खत दूरी पार करते रहे—बोस की जद्दोजहद की खबरें उज्जयंत की खामोश गलियारों तक पहुँचती रहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on Radha Kishore’s hands and a small casket
panels.action: A close view shows Radha Kishore Manikya’s hands opening a small ornate casket, revealing royal jewellery inside, while a trusted courtier waits to receive it respectfully.

dialogue.text: Biographies and Bose Institute traditions speak of Tripura royal funds—and even family jewellery—quietly pledged to sustain his experiments.

i18n.hi: जीवनियाँ और बोस इंस्टिट्यूट की परम्परा बताती है कि त्रिपुरा दरबार का धन—और यहाँ तक कि घर के गहने—चुपचाप उनकी प्रयोगशाला के नाम गिरवी रखे गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of discreet meeting in a palace side chamber
panels.action: In a dim side chamber, Radha Kishore Manikya hands a sealed envelope to a trusted emissary, his expression firm yet understated, suggesting an anonymous donation leaving the palace.

dialogue.text: “The giver need not be named; let the work speak,”

i18n.hi: “दाता का नाम ज़रूरी नहीं; काम खुद बोले,”

panels.shot: intercut shot between palace treasury and Calcutta lab
panels.action: Split composition: on one side, coins and jewellery are weighed in a palace treasury; on the other, a hand in a Calcutta laboratory carefully adjusts a new piece of apparatus on Bose’s bench.

dialogue.text: The tradition does not claim that Tripura built Bose’s science, only that its quiet rupees and ornaments helped keep his fragile research flame from going out.

i18n.hi: ये परम्परा ये दावा नहीं करती कि बोस की विज्ञान त्रिपुरा ने बनाई—बस इतना कि उसके चुप रुपये और गहनों ने उनकी नाज़ुक अनुसंधान ज्वाला को बुझने से बचाया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ujjayanta at night with a single lit window
panels.action: Ujjayanta Palace glows softly under the night sky; one window in an upper floor burns with lamplight, where Radha Kishore Manikya stands alone, gazing out thoughtfully.

dialogue.text: In one wing of Ujjayanta, the king balanced budgets for police and revenue; in another, he found room for grants that would never appear on public lists.

i18n.hi: उज्जयंत के एक हिस्से में राजा पुलिस और राजस्व के बजट तौलता रहा; दूसरे में, उसने उन अनुदानों के लिए जगह निकाली जो कभी किसी सरकारी सूची में नहीं दिखने वाले थे।

panels.shot: montage wide shot of later institutions
panels.action: A layered montage suggests later scenes: the Bose Institute building, students at Visva-Bharati under trees, and Ujjayanta Palace eventually serving as a state museum, all linked by a faint map line from Tripura to Bengal.

dialogue.text: Decades later, the Bose Institute, Visva-Bharati and the museum halls of Ujjayanta would stand as different answers to the same question: what should a kingdom build after an earthquake?

i18n.hi: दशकों बाद बोस इंस्टिट्यूट, विश्वभारती और उज्जयंत का म्यूज़ियम हाल उसी सवाल के अलग–अलग जवाब बनकर खड़े रहे—भूकम्प के बाद राज्य को क्या बनाना चाहिए?

panels.shot: close-up on Radha Kishore’s aged face fading into the palace façade
panels.action: An older Radha Kishore Manikya’s steady gaze fills the frame, subtly dissolving into the façade of Ujjayanta Palace, hinting at his legacy etched in stone and in unseen acts.

dialogue.text: Radha Kishore died in 1909, leaving behind a palace born from disaster, and a paper trail that hints at a king who saw science as part of statecraft.

i18n.hi: 1909 में राधा किशोर चल बसे, पीछे छोड़ गए एक महल जो आपदा से जन्मा था, और दस्तावेज़ों की ऐसी छाप जो एक ऐसे राजा की झलक देती है जो विज्ञान को राज्यकला का हिस्सा मानता था।

panels.shot: final reflective wide shot of modern Ujjayanta with visitors
panels.action: In the present day, visitors wander through Ujjayanta Palace’s courtyards and galleries; beyond them, a subtle overlay suggests a ghostly laboratory table, tying the building’s past to Bose’s era.

dialogue.text: Today, Ujjayanta stands as museum and memory, reminding us that after the earth shakes, a ruler can raise only walls—or also, in quiet, fund minds reaching for invisible waves and living cells.

i18n.hi: आज उज्जयंत म्यूज़ियम और याद दोनों है—याद दिलाता है कि ज़मीन हिलने के बाद शासक चाहे तो केवल दीवारें खड़ी कर सकता है, या फिर खामोशी में उन दिमागों को भी सहारा दे सकता है जो अदृश्य तरंगों और जीवित कोशिकाओं तक हाथ बढ़ाते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Radha Kishore Builds and Funds Science
title_i18n.hi: राधा किशोर: विज्ञान गढ़े, विज्ञान को सहारा दे

subtitle_i18n.en: From Shattered Palace to Silent Laboratory: A King’s Hidden Gift
subtitle_i18n.hi: टूटा महल, खामोश लैब: राजा का छुपा तोहफ़ा
